observations: ResourcePrivileges describes public/user/group allow/deny authorization; these inspected APIs do not establish granular READ-only TTL grant/revoke semantics.
ScopeManager.allowsManagedScope checks context owner or configuration accessRights.checkAuthorization, explicitly independent of parent federation membership.

RuntimeService.connectContext retrieves current configuration using the requesting UserScope and binds a request-derived identity; source does not justify copying an owner's credentials into a reader.

RuntimeServerController.closeContext delegates to RuntimeService.releaseContext, which checks allowsManagedScope before closing registered root. This generic ACL path is NOT proof of a native READ-versus-RELEASE distinction; do not run negative disposal tests against unrelated real roots.

No maintained deployed grant-management/TTL advertisement was established. New SDK calls require exact opt-in and matching sharedAccessProtocol advertisement; proposed experimental routes are not claimed existing Java endpoints.

Separate read-only native fixture test uses existing attach/query/point routes with explicit reader credentials; it does not prove the proposed grant protocol, native expiry, mutation denial or real scientific computation.
required_architectural_decision: Maintainer confirmation of granular context rights, principal/group issuer binding, grant/revoke/TTL transport and service incarnation/durable authorization semantics before native management compatibility can be claimed
fixture_limit: Explicit advertised ephemeral Runtime READ reference for two synthetic principals, max128 retained grants/tombstones, owner mutation only; no cross-service grants, federation rights, native Java ACL translation or persistence
